Arturo Aguiar
Argentina, Photographer
“I always carry a flashlight, to give light to whatever I find interesting, it’s been this way for over 20 years.”

Firstly through physics and later through art, I’ve always been interested in ways of knowing about and representing the world. Of all the ways which allow this kind of appreciation, light is one of the most important. We could even speak about a certain language of light that allows us to interpret what we see.

Art can be poetically described as a certain friction with reality, in the sense that something can be perceived differently, poetically, with other languages and grammar.

My work is based in the construction of photographic poetics. As all things poetic, it strives to subvert the codes and conventions of the language that conveys it. Photographic language, and the language of light.

The creation of such poetics surges from the possibility of taking pictures with lighting that differs from its natural language, and does not obey the laws of physics, but the whims and intuitions of a painter, which employs light only to caress the surfaces, objects and situations that are portrayed in a photograph.

The technique I use could be called “Photoluminic performance” or “painting of light”. In the darkness, I illuminate the scene manually, with flashlights in shots of long duration, creating with light a space of subjectivity which imprints stories onto images.

The use of light and color have a plastic and conceptual sense. Nothing can hide without lights and shadows. The contrasts between dazzling sparkles and darkness accentuate the mystery of all that is human, all that is beauty, and even, all that is terrible.
